entries.title: Joshua 10:3
segments: Hebron; south of Jerusalem.  The other places named are south-west of Jerusalem, in that part of Canaan which afterwards fell to the tribe of Judah.

entries.title: Joshua 10:4
segments: When sinners desert the cause of Satan and join with the people of God, those who continue to be Satan's slaves often unite against them, and would, if they could, utterly destroy them.

entries.title: Joshua 10:8
segments: Those who oppose their fellow men because they join the cause of God, oppose him, and thus often bring upon themselves utter ruin.

entries.title: Joshua 10:10
segments:
vv 10-11. 
 
  The way that goeth up to Beth-horon; literally, the way of the ascent of Beth-horon. 
 
  The going down to Beth-horon; the descent of Beth-horon.  There was an upper and lower Beth-horon, north-west of Jerusalem; and the pass between the two was called the ascent and the descent of Beth-horon. 
 
  Azekah; in the western plain of Judah.

entries.title: Joshua 10:11
segments: All the elements are under God's control, and when he directs will fight against his foes, as in the days of Moses, Barak, etc.

entries.title: Joshua 10:12
segments: Ajalon; a town and valley west of Gibeon.

entries.title: Joshua 10:13
segments: The book of Jasher; this is supposed by many to be a collection of poems, referring to the wonderful events in the history of Israel.

entries.title: Joshua 10:14
segments: Those who take the side of God, and follow his directions, will experience his aid, and through his grace will ultimately triumph.

entries.title: Joshua 10:15
segments: And Joshua returned--to Gilgal; these words are repeated in
.  The best explanation of them here is, that they stand at the close of a general summary of Joshua's victory, to which is immediately added a more particular account of the same proceedings. From
, it is manifest that it was in the midst of the pursuit that the report concerning the five kings was brought to Joshua.

entries.title: Joshua 10:16
segments: Makkedah; south-west of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Joshua 10:18
segments: Places to which the wicked flee for safety may become their prisons; and measures which they take to escape destruction, may be the occasion of bringing it upon them.

entries.title: Joshua 10:19
segments: The hindmost; such of them as they could overtake.

entries.title: Joshua 10:20
segments: Fenced; fortified.

entries.title: Joshua 10:22
segments: Those who have been most distinguished by the means of doing good, but have employed them in doing evil, will be most distinguished in their punishment.

entries.title: Joshua 10:24
segments: Upon the necks of these kings; in token of the complete victory of the Israelites over them and over all their foes.

entries.title: Joshua 10:29
segments: Libnah; a city south of Makkedah.

entries.title: Joshua 10:30
segments: Many things which are accomplished by human agency, are in the Bible ascribed to God.  In one sense man is the author, and in another sense God.

entries.title: Joshua 10:31
segments: Lachish; still further south.

entries.title: Joshua 10:33
segments: Gezer; in the territory that afterwards fell to the tribe of Ephraim, about fifteen miles north-west of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Joshua 10:34
segments: Eglon; a few miles west of Lachish.

entries.title: Joshua 10:36
segments: Hebron; a city east of Lachish, and twenty miles south of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Joshua 10:38
segments: Debir; southwest of Hebron.

entries.title: Joshua 10:40
segments: Country of the hills; the hill country of Judea and the southern part of Canaan.

By commanding the Israelites to destroy the Canaanites and take possession of their country, God laid them under obligation to do it; but no individual or nation, without his command, is authorized to do as they did.

entries.title: Joshua 10:41
segments:
Kadesh-barnea; near the south-east border of Canaan. 
 
  Gaza; near the Mediterranean and the south-west border of Canaan. 
 
  Goshen; lying south, in the mountainous region of Judea.
